data.raw_text:
DILG has again cancelled school and government office today at around 6:30 am.  No classes, no government work in Metro Manila National Capital Region and 16 provinces! 

By this time many were already on their way to work or school.  Many would not even have found out that school or work was cancelled until they arrived, because the weather is quite normal, and they would not have even suspected a cancellation was on the cards. 

How is the weather?  Overcast and scattered rain showers forecast today. So far nothing major for this time of year.  While flooding can be an issue in some areas, this happens if rain is very heavy.  Is heavy rain expected?  Not for my district.  Yet they have made widespread cancellations. 

Cancelling school and office comes at huge financial cost (has anyone quantified how much is lost by such an ad-lib declaration covering 17 provinces?), loss of learning for students forced to stay home (the general school system is already failing many students, what more with these ad-lib cancellations), lack of opportunity, lost productivity, inconvenience for parents and workers whose plans change last minute, and local and international reputation loss.  Failure of the government to provide the services they are paid by taxpayers to deliver due to closed offices. 

Many employees have no work, no pay and literally live from pay-day to pay-day with no reserves.  They and their families may go hungry with no work. 

This is the second government work and school cancellation in a week.  The last one was on 25 August 2025.  That day was also simply overcast with scattered showers.  Cancellation turned out to be an overreaction. 

Will today have been another over-reaction? 

The move to allow DILG to declare widespread school and work cancellations which was put in place last July is already backfiring badly.  Widespread cancellations are surely only justified for major typhoon events, not simple "inclement weather". 

Patience is wearing thin! 
https://t.co/WlpRqMuYcY
